# GrowthBook positioning & differentiators
Date: 2026-08-20 | Duration: 62m

## Summary
The team focused on identifying and refining three to four key differentiators for GrowthBook, emphasizing its developer-friendliness, open source nature, and warehouse-native architecture. Consensus was reached on important themes like flexibility, enterprise readiness, and innovation pace. Participants actively voted on differentiators, resulting in strong preferences for flexibility and AI-native capabilities. The discussion also highlighted the importance of deep customer partnerships and trust, along with a transparent pricing model that appeals to both enterprise clients and smaller users. AI was framed as a tool to enhance experimentation efficiency while retaining user control. Lastly, there was a commitment to create consistent messaging to support sales enablement and address both developer and non-technical user needs.

## Keywords
GrowthBook, differentiators, experimentation platform, developer-friendly, AI native, transparency, pricing flexibility

## Action Items

**Ashley Stirrup**
Lead follow-up working sessions with Elyse Fox and Scott Bailey to package and refine the elevator pitch and messaging pillars based on voting results and meeting insights (49:00)

**Elyse Fox**
Organize further discussions to elaborate on voting results, incorporate additional points discussed (e.g., modularity, partnership, transparency), and help draft the messaging framework (49:00)

**Scott Bailey**
Draft an initial elevator pitch script incorporating the top differentiators for internal review; develop supporting messaging architecture (50:17)

# GrowthBook positioning & differentiators
Date: 2026-09-17 | Duration: 41m

## Summary
The team agreed to position the platform as a platform for making the right product decisions and to avoid learning platform and product delivery language, which could create confusion with education, coding, hosting, or CI/CD tools. Messaging will emphasize AI-supported experimentation, targeted releases, rollout configuration, safety controls, and measurement rather than the entire product lifecycle. The group preferred Built and Ship and ship and measure over build and run, while planning speaker notes and aligned sales talk tracks. Sales collateral will retain a 24-logo grid but remove inactive or low-value customers, verify paying-customer status, manage approvals and confidentiality, and enlarge priority brands. Christian Liebenow will present the revised AI slides, Ashley Stirrup will coordinate sales alignment, and Elyse Fox and Luke Sonnet will refine slide text and logo layouts. Updates are to be completed before the next major sales push, with adoption and refinement estimated at about 7 months.

## Keywords
GrowthBook, product decisions, AI experimentation, product lifecycle, sales messaging, logo review

## Action Items

**Christian Liebenow**
Prepare and present the updated AI product lifecycle slide focusing on AI aspects at the next company meeting (28:30)

**Elyse Fox**
Add speaker notes to slides to clarify AI contributions across the product lifecycle for sales teams (15:12)
Revise logos on sales decks by removing outdated or non-paying customer logos and resizing remaining logos for better clarity and impact (20:05)
Investigate better versions or alternatives for problematic logos such as Leo Vegas to improve visual quality in sales decks (27:29)

**Unassigned**
Align sales and marketing messaging to emphasize 'platform for making the right product decisions' and 'AI for experimentation-driven product development' in all sales collateral and presentations (07:00)
Refine lifecycle slide language by replacing 'suggest' with stronger verbs like 'identify' and changing 'build and run' to 'ship and measure' to better reflect GrowthBook's focus (09:44)
Follow up with Character AI regarding contract and usage status to confirm whether to include or exclude their logo in sales decks (21:34)
